subject: Dedicated capacity: benchmark results + commit/pricing proposal

Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing — initial loadtest + questions

Hi Michael / Ellen —

Thanks again for sharing your expected traffic profiles last week. We ran a focused Dedicated-capacity load test against a realistic replica of your prompt mix and session distribution. Attached are the summary PDF and raw TPS traces. High-level findings:

- Sustained peak TPS observed (90th percentile across 1h window): 42 TPS for gen-heavy sessions.
- Average token latency at that load (p50/p95): 120ms / 490ms using our 8xA100 pool profile.
- KV cache hit rate variable because of many short sessions — we saw ~18% effective caching which reduced token compute per request less than expected.

To size a Dedicated GPU pool with a 99% availability/95th latency SLO similar to what you described, we estimate you need a baseline of 12xA100 equivalent GPUs with capacity for 30% burst headroom (can be filled via burst credits or autoscale).

Questions to confirm before we finalize pricing:
1) Are you comfortable with a 95th latency SLO ~500ms for gen flows, or should we target a stricter 350ms SLO?
2) Do you expect traffic to be spiky (bursts >3x baseline) during seasonal events?
3) Would you prefer a monthly reserved commit (offers best unit price) or a quarterly ramped commit with stepdowns?

See attached for raw traces and the TPS-to-GPU mapping we used. If helpful I can schedule a 30-min walkthrough with Vivek (SE) to go through traces and the proposed GPU allocation.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Thanks Marissa — quick technical notes / caveats from the SE side:

On Sun, 8 Mar 2026 at 09:12, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> High-level findings:
> - Sustained peak TPS observed (90th percentile across 1h window): 42 TPS for gen-heavy sessions.
> - Average token latency at that load (p50/p95): 120ms / 490ms using our 8xA100 pool profile.

- The 42 TPS number is for your current prompt templates (avg prompt tokens ~220). If you start expanding to longer context (500+ tokens) the per-request GPU occupancy increases non-linearly; expect ~30-40% capacity drop.
- Our concurrency model relies on continuous batching + KV caching. Given your short-lived sessions, enabling sticky routing (session pinning) reduces cold KV misses and will improve p95 by ~80-120ms in practice. We measured that in the attached traces (look for the annotation sv=sticky ON/OFF).
- For headroom we recommend committing to a baseline that covers 1.5x your current 90th TPS (so ~63 TPS in our model) if you want to avoid throttling during 15–30 minute bursts. That maps to ~18xA100 equivalent for sustained low-latency SLOs.

Pricing-wise:
- Monthly reserved commit for 12 GPUs: baseline price X (Marissa will share numbers) with a 15% committed discount.
- Step-up quarterly commit for 18 GPUs: better for seasonally-spiky workloads; effective blended discount ~18% if you commit 12->18 over 2 quarters.

I'll be available for a walkthrough Tuesday afternoon if you want to go line-by-line.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni, Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Marissa / Vivek —

Thanks for the quick run and notes. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Latency SLO: Our product team wants 95th <= 350ms for the customer-facing generate path. 500ms is safer but could impact UX. Is the 350ms target realistic without doubling the GPU count?
2) Traffic profile: we expect periodic spikes tied to marketing campaigns — bursts up to 4x baseline for 10–20 minutes, maybe 2–3 times per quarter.
3) Contract preference: we prefer to start with a quarterly ramp (12 -> 18) to avoid over-committing in Q1. But we need predictable unit costs for budget planning.

Also: can you give an explicit example of pricing (monthly $) for the 12gpu commit vs 18gpu ramp, and what discount tiers apply at 12/18/24? We will share this with Procurement.

-Michael

Michael —

Appreciate the detail. Below is a concrete pricing illustration and the optional contract structures. I kept the numbers as monthly committed spend (USD) for clarity — final contract will show annualized commit and billing cadence.

Option A — Monthly price for a steady commit (12xA100-equivalent):
- Unit list: $9,900 per GPU per month -> baseline list $118,800/month
- Committed discount (12-month commit): 15% -> $100,980/month
- Included burst credits: 20% (first 6 months) after which burst is pay-as-you-go at on-demand rates.

Option B — Quarterly ramping commit (12 -> 18 over 2 quarters):
- Q1 (12 GPUs): 15% discount -> $100,980/month
- Q2 (18 GPUs): 18% effective blended discount applied to the increased commit -> est $153,000/month
- If you hit 4x burst windows we recommend enabling our autoscale buffer rather than permanently committing to 24 GPUs; autoscale pricing applies only during ramp windows.

Option C — 24 GPU long-term commit (best unit economics):
- 22% discount -> est $186,000/month (if you know you'll consistently need 4x headroom).

Latency/throughput notes (short):
- 350ms p95 for your current prompts is achievable but requires the 18-GPU sustained profile or the 12 GPU + aggressive sticky routing + significant burst capacity. Our conservative recommendation is to plan for 18 GPUs for a production-grade 350ms p95 at 90th/peak TPS.

Next steps I propose:
1) Vivek to run one more targeted test with session pinning enabled to quantify p95 improvement (we can do this Tue 11:00 PT).
2) If results align, we prepare a quarter-by-quarter commit schedule and a draft SOW for Procurement to review.

Laura — can you drop the procurement checklist and PO template? Dev — looping you for any legal/term constraints on burst pricing.

Thanks,
Marissa
